blocks.content: I eat half a banana over the sink before I run, because I run better with something in my stomach and I run worse if I think about it too hard. So I eat the banana before I'm fully awake and we never speak of it again.

My mom thinks I should eat a real breakfast. My mom also thinks I should be taking at least one class somewhere, which, noted, I am getting there, but the banana is my compromise position and it works well enough.

Shoes go on in a specific order. Left first, then right. Not superstition — just the order I've always done it in, and I see no reason to introduce chaos into a system that works. I lace them the way my dad taught me when I was seven. It's the only thing I still do the way my dad taught me. I don't think about that.

Before I left I walked a slow loop through the apartment. Not because I forget things. I don't forget things. Just — I like to see it before I go. The shelf of paints. The brushes standing in their jars. The sketchbook open on the desk, pencil resting in the crease.
My mom sees order. I see all the things I came back to yesterday. There's a difference.
I locked the door. Headed down the stairs.
